options: A command that resets all GPU memory to zero
A collective operation that combines a value from every participant and returns the combined result to all of them
A method for compressing model weights before saving
A single GPU broadcasting data without receiving anything back
questions.explain: An all-reduce combines values (like gradients) contributed by every participant and ensures every participant ends up with the same combined (e.g. averaged) result.

options: NVIDIA's library implementing collective GPU-to-GPU communication operations like all-reduce
A tool for monitoring GPU temperature
A CUDA compiler optimization flag
A replacement for the PyTorch autograd engine
questions.explain: NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library) implements collective communication operations — all-reduce, broadcast, all-gather, reduce-scatter — tuned to exploit NVLink/NVSwitch topology when available.

questions.q: What problem does a naive (single-GPU-collects-everything) all-reduce have?
options: It cannot average floating-point numbers correctly
It requires the CPU to perform all computation
The collecting GPU becomes a bottleneck, the same issue DataParallel has
It only works with exactly two GPUs
questions.explain: Having one GPU collect, average, and broadcast results back creates a bottleneck at that single GPU — the same structural problem DataParallel has.

questions.q: How does ring all-reduce avoid a single bottleneck node?
options: By using only the CPU for all communication
By having every GPU communicate directly with every other GPU simultaneously
By disabling gradient synchronization entirely
By arranging GPUs in a logical ring where each one only exchanges data with its immediate neighbor, passing partial sums around
questions.explain: In ring all-reduce, GPUs are logically arranged in a ring and each one only ever communicates with its immediate neighbor, passing partial sums around until every GPU has the complete result — no GPU does disproportionate work.

questions.q: What does setting the environment variable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO do?
options: It logs which transport (such as NVLink) NCCL chose for each communication channel
It forces NCCL to use only PCIe regardless of available hardware
It disables NCCL entirely for debugging purposes
It increases the batch size automatically
questions.explain: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO makes NCCL print logging information, including which transport it selected for each communication channel, letting you confirm whether NVLink or a slower fallback path is actually being used.
